title: Cutty sarks
html_source:
“Cutty sark)” is 18th-century Scots for “short chemise” or “short undergarment”.

Hyphenated, Cutty-sark was a nickname given to the witch Nannie Dee, a fictional character created by Robert Burns in his Tam o' Shanter, after the garment she wore. The figurehead of the tea clipper Cutty Sark is named after the character and a brand of Scotch whisky is named in turn for the ship.

For more elaborate etymology, see link, but essentially chemise -> witch -> ship -> whiskey
